main_text.p: militudine. Quasi vero Clemens, longè post datam ad Hebræos Epistolam Corinthios compellaturus, non potuerit sibi hanc proponere imitandam? Aut Epistolæ illius fuisse ipsemet Græcus interpres? In eo præterea omnis affinitas, quod suam Clemens, variis alterius Epistolæ sententijs & dictis, quæ ad institutum suum facerent, exornavit. De cætero, omninò discrepat stylus, & ut Græca magis est phrasis Clementis, sic illa Epistolæ ad Hebræos magis mixta, & Hebræam redolens sæpissimè eloquentiam.

VIII. Secundò, verba sunt Eusebij, Τῆς [?] πρὸς Ἑβραίους [?] πολλὰ νοήματα [?] ἤδη δὲ [illegible, ~10 letters]. Jugulum petit, quod hanc, Clemens suæ Epistolæ aliquoties intexat, usurpet, causas suæ obtendat. Planè, ut Polycarpus, & Ignatius, Scripturæ phrases, & enunciata, ad majorem sive elegantiam, sive ἐνέργειαν, intertexere suis Epistolis solent. Sed ille longè plura, testibus Eusebio & Hieronymo, ut

page.notes: The Greek line at the end of the first paragraph of the second block is only partly legible in the scan; uncertain words are marked [?] and the rest is marked illegible. The word "ἐνέργειαν" is read from a small print and may be imprecise. The catchword "Epi-" is the start of the next page. Greek in "Ignatius" and "Polycarpus" is printed in roman type, not Greek. The text is printed as "Scripturæ phrases", with the printed spelling retained.
